meta.title: Cadente — the hub where everything is a plugin, even the AI
meta.description: Cadente is a free desktop app that brings agents such as Claude Code and Codex, a terminal, an API client, a database client, notes and a calendar into one split window. Everything is a plugin, even the AI. Built in Rust, for Mac, Windows and Linux, in 15 languages.
meta.ogDescription: The hub where everything is a plugin, even the AI: agents, terminal, database and notes in one window.

hero.eyebrow: Free · Mac, Windows and Linux · built in Rust · 15 languages
hero.lede: Agents, terminal, database, notes and calendar in the same window, all from the keyboard. Every part is a plugin: keep what you use, swap what you want and turn off the rest, even the AI. And it costs nothing.
hero.sub: Everything is a plugin. Even the AI.

creator.title:
Your plugin
can become income.
creator.lede: Had an idea that fixes your day? It probably fixes other people's too. Describe it to the agent, it writes the plugin, you publish it in the store and choose how to charge. You keep 90% of donations and 70% of sales and of every subscription renewal.
creator.donationText: The plugin is free, and people who like it can support you.
creator.subscriptionText: Monthly or yearly. You earn on every renewal, not just the first.
creator.onceText: People pay once and use it on up to 5 computers.
creator.trialText: Let people try it for a few days before you charge.

calc.note: This is an estimate, before taxes and card fees. It is calculated on the net amount, and every sale goes through the Cadente checkout.

creator.makerTitle: From idea to store, without leaving Cadente.
creator.makerLede: Three example requests, each earning a different way: a pet Cadu loose on the screen, a dashboard with today's sales and a status page that tells you when GitHub, Cloudflare or AWS go down. You can drag Cadu around, feed him and give him a bath.
creator.step1Text: A Chat opens with the request. Nothing is sent until you press <kbd>↵</kbd>.
creator.step2Text: Manifest, code and tests, in a pane next to where you are.
creator.step3Text: cadente plugin dev runs the plugin right there, next to the conversation. Cadu lives loose on top of the app: drag him, press f to feed him and b for a bath.
creator.step4Text: /publish and that's it: it is in the store, at the price you chose.

rust.title:
Rust from the core
to the screen.
The fan never kicks in.
rust.lede: No hidden browser and no Node running behind it. Cadente is native, Rust from the core to the interface, and drawn by the GPU.
rust.stack: cadente ├─ core rust ├─ interface rust · slint, drawn by the GPU ├─ terminal rust · native pty ├─ agents rust · claude, codex, agy and any cli └─ plugins rust · webassembly for community ones
rust.memoryText: History stays on disk and only loads when you open it. The app does not grow over time.
rust.batteryText: The interface talks straight to the core, with no local server or browser in between.
rust.hiddenText: Close the pane and it is gone. No terminal, agent or plugin keeps running behind it.

plugins.title:
Every pane becomes
what you need.
plugins.lede: Chat, Terminal, Workspaces, Requests, Calendar, Focus: the built-in plugins all work the same way. <kbd>↵</kbd> opens, <kbd>.</kbd> shows what you can do, <kbd>/</kbd> lists the commands, <kbd>⇥</kbd> switches the view. Learn one and you know them all. Click one to see it.
plugins.communityText: The store opens soon: anyone can publish, and installing is always free. Don’t use AI? Keep only the productivity ones.

owner.title:
Even the AI
is a plugin.
owner.lede: The Chat, the Terminal, the sidebar, the AI provider, even the theme: every part of Cadente is a plugin, just like the community ones. Swap the provider, turn off what you don’t use and, if you like, turn off the AI and keep a hub with a terminal, database, notes and calendar.
owner.installText: From a link or a folder, without restarting anything.
owner.removeText: The built-in plugins turn off too.
owner.swapText: Swap the provider and the plugins that depend on it restart on the new one.
owner.layer1Text: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode or the CLI you already use.
owner.layer2Text: Your subscription, an API key or a local model in Ollama.
owner.layer3Text: Turn it on, off or swap it without restarting the app.
owner.layer4Text: Even the sidebar and the theme are plugins.
owner.noAiText: Turn off the AI and the rest keeps working: terminal, workspaces, notes, database and calendar.

store.title:
If someone needed it,
someone built it.
store.lede: Kanban, Kubernetes, lo-fi radio, a board for diagrams. The store opens soon, installing costs nothing and most plugins will be free. The plugins below are examples.
store.empty: No plugin with that name yet. Why not build yours?
store.oneClickText: It downloads, checks the file is the right one and installs.
store.openText: Published on GitHub with the cadente-plugin topic? Your plugin is in the store.
store.watchedText: If a malicious plugin shows up, it is blocked and turns itself off on every machine.

finale.title:
Ready to open
the first pane?
finale.lede: It’s free, runs on Mac, Windows and Linux, speaks 15 languages and asks for no card.

morning.title: 9 am. The day is already set up.
morning.text: You open Cadente and the first pane already shows the day: the daily at 9:30, the design meeting at 2 pm and a merge conflict waiting. No need to open five apps to know where to start. <kbd>⇥</kbd> moves to the recent items and the tasks.

claude.title: First, a test for Claude.
claude.text: ⌘O and four letters turn the pane into a Terminal. You open Claude Code with the subscription you already pay for and ask for a test for focus_neighbor. It starts writing, and you move on to the next one.

agents.title: Three agents, not one extra window.
agents.text: ⌘D splits the screen sideways and ⌘⇧D downwards. Codex runs the tests, agy explains layout.rs, and under Claude there is still a Terminal left for you. All working, all in sight.

ci.title: Then the login CI breaks.
ci.text: A new page shows the four open branches and the state of each PR. Login is red. You open the branch and <kbd>⌘J</kbd> brings up a Chat that already knows where you are, so you just ask why. The diff opens next to it.

api.title: Now, the feature of the day.
api.text: Today's task is the projects API. In Requests you open GET /v1/projects, change limit to 5 and send it. Then the POST creates the showcase project. The agents keep going on the first page, and you never opened another program.

store.title: A database client is missing.
store.text: To check that the POST was saved, you need to look at the database. The Store opens right below: you find Postgres, flip through the screenshots, check what it asks to access and install it with <kbd>↵</kbd>, for free.

db.title: The database confirms the POST.
db.text: <kbd>⌘↵</kbd> runs the select under the cursor. In the projects query, the showcase project is already there. You change the order right on the line, run it again and open the sessions table from the database browser.

app.title: And it already shows in the app.
app.text: On a new page, the Browser opens the app you are building, at localhost:5173. The showcase project is in the list. ↓ walks through the links, ↵ opens the project and ⌫ goes back.

diagram.title: A diagram for the meeting.
diagram.text: The design meeting is at 2 pm. Next to the site, you install Board from the Store and draw the path of the data, without opening another tool. <kbd>r</kbd> makes a rectangle, <kbd>o</kbd> an ellipse and <kbd>a</kbd> connects the two.

meeting.title: In the meeting, the notes become tasks.
meeting.text: The notes live in Documents, as a .md file in your folder. You write the next tasks right in the text, <kbd>↵</kbd> starts the next one and <kbd>space</kbd> checks off the one already done: the blog announcement.

focus.title: Then, 25 minutes of focus.
focus.text: A page just for you: the calendar, a 25-minute pomodoro, the computer's memory and how much of Claude you have used. <kbd>⌘1</kbd> to <kbd>⌘6</kbd> jump between the six pages of the day.

accounts.title: Use the subscriptions you already pay for.
accounts.text: Usage showed Claude at 58% of its limit. Settings has the accounts you already own: Claude Max, ChatGPT Plus, a Gemini key, OpenRouter and a local model in Ollama. Each conversation picks its own, and Cadente charges nothing on top.

plugins.title: What you don't use, goes.
plugins.text: In Plugins, even the built-in ones can go. <kbd>space</kbd> turns off Links and Tools. The AI provider can be swapped too: it moves to Ollama, on your laptop, and you see what changes first. You can turn off the AI entirely.

end.title: End of the day. Who is still waiting?
end.text: <kbd>⌘⇧A</kbd> gathers the agents from every page, with whoever is waiting at the top. Claude still asks permission to save the test: <kbd>↵</kbd> takes you to it and <kbd>y</kbd> allows it. Every plugin you used today was made by someone, and the next one could be yours.

agents.title:
Your agents,
side by side.
agents.lede: Cadente doesn’t replace your agent. Claude Code, Codex and the other CLIs run as they are, with your account. Cadente organizes the work around them: each task in its own worktree, all of them in sight, and whoever needs you shows up first.
agents.any: And any other CLI that runs in a terminal.
agents.p1Text: Each agent works on its own branch and in its own directory, without touching the other’s files.
agents.p2Text: <kbd>⌘⇧A</kbd> gathers the agents from every page, with whoever needs you at the top.
agents.p3: The subscription you already pay for
agents.p3Text: Claude Max, ChatGPT Plus, an API key or a local model. Cadente charges nothing on top.
agents.p4Text: Calls go from your machine to the provider you chose. No Cadente server sits in the middle.
agents.p5Text: Sessions, history and settings live in a local database, on your computer.

faq.title:
Before you
download.
faq.q1: Is it just a wrapper around Claude Code?
faq.a1: No. Claude Code, Codex and the other CLIs run in Cadente’s terminal as they are, with your account. Cadente is the window around them: it splits the screen into panes, gives each task a worktree, gathers the agents waiting for you and puts a terminal, database, API client, notes and calendar next to them.
faq.q2: How is it different from running Claude Code in a terminal?
faq.a2: For the agent, it isn’t: it is the same CLI. The difference is around it. Several agents work side by side, each in its own worktree, ⌘⇧A shows who is waiting for you, and the rest of your work stays in the same window.
faq.q3: Do my calls go through your servers?
faq.a3: No. Cadente talks straight to the provider you chose, with your subscription or your key. Cadente’s server only keeps your account.
faq.a4: It does. The AI is a plugin like the others: turn it off and keep the terminal, workspaces, notes, database and calendar.
faq.q5: If it’s free, how do you make money?
faq.a5: From the plugin store, once it opens: Cadente keeps 30% of sales and subscriptions and 10% of donations. The app stays free.
faq.a6: 15: Portuguese, English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Russian, Turkish, Arabic, Hindi, Indonesian, Vietnamese, Japanese, Korean and Simplified Chinese. Switching is instant, with no restart. Some new screens arrive in Portuguese and English first.
faq.a7: macOS, on Apple Silicon and Intel, plus Windows and Linux, both on x64.
